headline: Robotics startup Generalist reaches $3B valuation, sources say
summary: The AI robotics firm secured nearly $200 million in fresh capital, extending its Series B to $600 million and boosting its valuation from $2 billion just months ago.
details: Robotics startup Generalist is now valued at $3 billion, according to sources familiar with the funding. This comes after raising nearly $200 million in additional capital, primarily led by 8VC.
This new funding extends their Series B round, bringing the total for that round to $600 million. Generalist had previously announced a $400 million Series B in June at a $2 billion valuation.

Founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind and Boston Dynamics engineers, Generalist develops an AI foundation model for various robots. Its Gen 1.5 model reportedly allows robots to learn new tasks from video demonstrations as short as 3 to 12 seconds.

The startup has been operating quietly, working with a few customers to tailor its model for specific use cases. Early backers include 8VC, Radical Ventures, Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Bezos Expeditions, and AI researcher Fei-Fei Li.

Generalist faces competition from other firms also building general robot brains, such as Physical Intelligence (reportedly valued at $11 billion) and SoftBank-backed Skild AI (valued at $14 billion). Genesis AI is also reportedly seeking capital at a $3 billion valuation.

This surge in funding reflects investor belief in a potential "ChatGPT moment" for robotics, where robots can perform general tasks without explicit training. However, some VCs caution that a truly general robotics model might still be years away due to data limitations.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI loses top data center exec]] Chris Malone amid ongoing executive churn
headline: OpenAI loses top data center exec Chris Malone amid ongoing executive churn
summary: Chris Malone, former head of data centers, left OpenAI last week. His departure is significant as data center strategy is crucial for AI infrastructure, amid a string of other high-profile exits.
details: OpenAI's former head of data centers, Chris Malone, departed last week, as reported by the Wall Street Journal. Malone, who previously worked at Meta and Google, joined OpenAI in March of last year, making his tenure relatively short.
Malone's arrival followed the launch of Project Stargate, a $500 million data center initiative in the U.S. OpenAI is a key partner in this effort, alongside Oracle, Nvidia, SoftBank, and Microsoft.

The reason for Malone's departure is not entirely clear, but OpenAI stated it recently "reorganized" its "infrastructure organization." The company emphasized its "strong, deeply experienced data center team" remains in place.

As part of the reorganization, Malone's reporting structure changed; he began reporting to OpenAI VP Sachin Katti instead of President Greg Brockman. Several other executives now oversee the data center strategy.
These include Uday Ruddarraju, leading the data center team; Brent Mayo, heading the build and delivery program; and Spas Lazarov, leading all data center engineering.

Malone's exit is part of a broader trend, adding to over a dozen executive departures this year. Business Insider recently tallied 13 exits in 2026, with several senior leaders leaving in the past month alone.

Recent high-profile departures include Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser, who left after eight months, and Brad Lightcap, a long-serving Chief Operating Officer, who announced he's "starting something new."

Fidji Simo, the former product and business chief who reported directly to Sam Altman, also stepped down due to a "chronic illness" but remains in an advisory role. The safety and ethics teams have also seen notable exits.
Other leaders, like Bill Peebles (former head of Sora), left due to project shutdowns, while Chief Marketing Officer Kate Rouch also reportedly departed for health reasons.

OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman has attributed the scrutiny of departures to the company's intense "spotlight." However, the churn raises questions, especially with its IPO reportedly pushed to 2027 and concerns about valuation.
